title: Signal quality assessment for single-lead wearable ECG: a survey and comparative study

record.title: Signal quality assessment for single-lead wearable ECG: a survey and comparative study
record.abstract: Reliable automatic interpretation of single-lead wearable ECG recordings is contingent upon accurate signal quality assessment (SQA), yet no consensus exists on the best methodology for this task. This survey reviews 38 SQA algorithms published between 2010 and 2022, categorizing them by feature type (statistical, spectral, template-based, and learned), classification strategy, and target application domain. We implement and comparatively evaluate nine representative approaches on two independent ECG datasets collected with chest-worn patches under both controlled and free-living conditions. Evaluation metrics include per-segment quality classification accuracy, computational cost on an ARM Cortex-M4 platform, and downstream impact on AF detector performance when SQA-based segment rejection is applied as a pre-processing gate. Results show that lightweight spectral flatness combined with kurtosis achieves the best accuracy-to-cost trade-off for real-time embedded use, while deep-learning approaches yield superior accuracy at much higher computational expense. The survey concludes with a discussion of open challenges including cross-device generalization and labelling inconsistencies across public datasets.
